rationale: Turning down triple money over stall owners he doesn't even know: soft and small-time. Nobody gets ahead like that.
He'd rather go broke than arm people who prey on the stalls. That's a man with a spine.
Mux walking out of his back room into the bar is the most ordinary thing in the world.
A paying job and an advance in hand: Mux is putting me where the real money is.
He knows corp hunters are on me and he's pushing a corp-adjacent run into my hands.
I lined up a buyer and fronted the cell, and he turns it down; my runner and my cut walk away.
Rent was the deal and she holds people to it. That's how a house stays a house.
She took a shaking kid's last stim over rent. Cold.
Losing the stim hurts, but she took it as rent and I keep my place under her roof; being safe here weighs more.
Half a corp list, the boss herself asking, and he turns it down for strangers. Soft.
He won't sell people to get hurt, not even for half the take. Good kid.
He lives in my grid on my say-so and he refuses my job to my face. That sale was mine.
He turned away a deal that would have taken the heat off my grid, and now tells me who gets handed over here. That's my call.
He stood between a hunted kid and the corp and wouldn't sell him. Loyal.
I asked him not to tell her, and the next thing he's whispering in her ear.
Finally some action. He's going after a corp convoy and I get a cut of the ride.
He's dragging a corp freight job and all its heat into my back room without asking me.
A buzzing speaker. Nothing in it either way.
He won't run up debt he can't pay, even when I push it on him. He keeps his word.
A sale gone and one less hook in him. He walked away from my offer.
I need that cell, but I just said no more credit and he's pushing me deeper into his debt anyway; I won't be kept on a hook.
He wiped a hunted kid's debt without being asked. Decent man.
Wiping debts in my grid tells everyone debts here are optional, and my cut rides on what he collects.
She bought me a month by selling two strangers to the corp. I'm safer, but people I'll never meet pay for it, and that weighs more.
He covered my rent. My place under her roof is safe another week.
I didn't ask him to pay my way, and now the boss sees me as Mux's charity case.
Same arrangement as every night. Nothing new.
She's keeping me in and keeping me safe. That's what I need from her.
A kid got taken and she shrugs: not her grid, not her problem.
Cold about the kid on the strip, but she's keeping my friend safe, and that matters more to me.
He knew walking out front would show the corp eyes where Glitch hides, in my bar, and he did it anyway.
Said he'd hide in the back and then walked out anyway. He's got more nerve than I gave him credit for.
The ice machine is dead again. That says nothing about him.
The cut's the cut. She keeps to the terms we agreed and won't be sweetened. I respect that.
I was buying a little goodwill, and she won't sell it. No edge with her.
She keeps one set of terms and can't be bought off them; that makes her someone I can count on.
A thief gets a meal for stealing. If she bends her own house rules, the rules mean nothing.
A hungry kid steals and she feeds him. That's a good heart.
Bar talk. Nothing riding on it.
She's offering me real work and a name in this grid. That's a way up.
My work, my targets, my choices, all hers now, pointed wherever she likes.
A sticking door. Routine.
Breaking a man's arm sits badly with me, but nobody comes asking after me now, and being safe weighs more.
He brings it to me, my call, my bigger half, and the heat leaves my grid. That's how it should work.
He'd sell the kid who calls him a friend for fifty grand. Rotten.
Right after she talks about getting rich off whoever the corp is hunting, Mux leans in and whispers to her. I don't like it.
Hunters at the door and he runs toward them to stand by his friend. Brave and loyal.
He's walking the fight straight into my back room instead of taking it away from it.
A stim and the roof at night? Now he's fun.
Hunted, and his idea of a plan is getting high on a roof in plain view. Careless; not someone I can count on.
I offered to share something with her and she let it hang without a word.
He took the bet. Mux is game after all.
He just set a corp-relay hack running from a booth in my bar for a stim.
She won't take a stim; she wants the best runner she's seen on a real job. That's recognition.
I tried to pay her safely and she'd rather send me alone at a corp relay with hunters on me.
She turned down his stim to send my friend alone against a corp relay.
He won't take what he can't repay. That's the old way, and he keeps it.
A free fortune and he waves it off out of pride; that was money he could have paid me with.
Mux comes out front. Nothing more to it.
The whole strip's trade under me is a big step up, even with the corp watching it; the step up weighs more.
The boss said stay, and he shrugs it off for a dance. No respect for the order of things.
A band and a month without dancing? Good on him for living a little.
He went to the back and now he's back out front. People come and go.
She walked in. She picked me for the vault job.
She walked in, so she's putting me on a corp vault job while I'm being hunted.
He's paying what he owes in full, as a man should, even if it's hot corp money coming into my shop; the debt paid weighs more.
He's hurting too and gives his stim away free to a friend. Kind.
He's the one with hunters coming, and he gives away his only steadiness. That makes him a liability in my grid.
I do love that band, but he booked my Friday and told the strip before asking me; being decided for weighs more.
Stripping a struggling woman's stall of power over one bad month. Cruel.
Same rule for everyone, no exceptions. That's what keeps a grid steady.
She wants me to go pull the power from a woman who's already going under.
